lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Brock Purdy carves up the Vikings' D with 3 TD passes in the 49ers' 35-10 win in Mexico City
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: MEXICO CITY -- — Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers offense turned the much ballyhooed matchup between one of the game's top offenses and the stingiest defenses into a one-sided affair.  Purdy carved up Minnesota with three touchdown passes in the first half and the 49ers beat the Vikings 35-10 Sunday night in a matchup of NFC powerhouses.  “You have to be aggressive and don’t second-guess yourself,” Purdy said.  “Obviously try to read it out the best you can, but when you have players that can go get the ball, allow them to go and make plays. ” Cousins lost for the second time in three weeks against the Niners, also throwing a pick-6 in Week 9 for the Raiders in his final start before being traded back to Minnesota.

injuryReport.name: Quenton Nelson
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

injuryReport.name: Abraham Lucas
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

injuryReport.name: Jarran Reed
injuryReport.beatComment: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

injuryReport.beatComment: Smith-Njigba previously has been listed on Seattle injury reports this season for rest purposes, but this marks the first time his practice reps were impacted by a health concern. He'll have two more days to increase his activity level this week, with Friday's practice report set to reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco.

injuryReport.name: Sam Darnold
injuryReport.beatComment: Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level of health.

irReserve.name: George Holani
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

coachingMatchup.headline: Kyle Shanahan & DC Raheem Morris vs. HC Mike Macdonald, OC Brian Fleury & DC Aden Durde (Levi's Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Kyle Shanahan's 21-personnel motion attack and DC Raheem Morris's split-safety defense against Seattle Seahawks (6-4)—testing both San Francisco's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and secondary consistency.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Kyle Shanahan pairs 21 personnel and condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to diagnose Seattle Seahawks's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the 12-to-22 yard honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts between the numbers.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Seattle Seahawks's gap-scheme pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Raheem Morris holds disguised two-high shells before spinning into Quarters, Cover 6, or cloud-trap while balancing four-man pass-rush pressure and red-zone coverage discipline.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion rate and red-zone touchdown efficiency determine whether San Francisco controls possession length or lets Seattle Seahawks's front dictate obvious passing downs and compressed-field spacing.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Levi's Stadium game-script management, penalty discipline, and hidden special-teams field position shape late-game leverage on both sidelines.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Brock Purdy, George Kittle & Deebo Samuel Sr. vs. CB Devon Witherspoon & LB Drake Thomas
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #6 Pass Off (255.5 yds) · #1 Off. Scoring (+12.78) | SEA: #4 Pass Def (-3.19)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Brock Purdy, George Kittle & Deebo Samuel Sr. attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Seattle Seahawks's #4 pass defense (-3.19). Winning early-down timing throws keeps San Francisco's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Brock Purdy (#13) scanning Seahawks's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Drake Thomas widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for George Kittle (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: DeForest Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa & Nick Bosa vs. QB Sam Darnold & C Jalen Sundell
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | SEA: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: DeForest Buckner, Osa Odighizuwa & Nick Bosa lead San Francisco's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Seattle Seahawks's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets 49ers keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether DeForest Buckner (#99) draw chip help from Seahawks's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Osa Odighizuwa (#92).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Fred Warner, Deommodore Lenoir & Renardo Green vs. WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba & QB Sam Darnold
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #16 Pass Def (+1.78) | SEA: #17 Pass Off (218.5 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Fred Warner, Deommodore Lenoir & Renardo Green anchor San Francisco's #16 pass defense (+1.78) against WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Seattle Seahawks's #17 passing attack (218.5 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Seahawks into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Fred Warner (#54) at the top of routes against WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Sam Darnold's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Christian McCaffrey & Kyle Juszczyk vs. Seahawks Front Seven & LB Drake Thomas
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #5 Rush Off (138.6 yds) | SEA: #8 Rush Def (-1.40)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Christian McCaffrey & Kyle Juszczyk test Seattle Seahawks's #8 run defense (-1.40) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Seahawks's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Seahawks's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Christian McCaffrey (#23).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Connor Colby, Dominick Puni & Jake Brendel vs. DT Byron Murphy II & Seahawks Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SF: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | SEA: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Connor Colby, Dominick Puni & Jake Brendel protect Brock Purdy (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Byron Murphy II and Seattle Seahawks's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Connor Colby (#75) on obvious passing downs—if DT Byron Murphy II cannot win clean around the arc, Seahawks must dial up interior stunts that stress Dominick Puni (#77).
